nodes.name: Elliptic Monge-Ampere equation with Dirichlet boundary condition
nodes.statement: \det (D^2 u) = f \text{ in } \Omega, \quad u=g \text{ on } \partial \Omega,
nodes.label: MA

nodes.name: Convex polygonal domain and smooth strictly convex solution
nodes.statement: The domain $\Omega$ is assumed to be a convex polygonal domain of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and \eqref{MA} is assumed to have a strictly convex smooth solution $u \in C^3(\tir{\Omega})$.

nodes.name: Regularity of the data f and g
nodes.statement: The function $f \in C^1(\tir{\Omega})$ is given and satisfies $f \geq c_0$ for a constant $c_0 >0$ and the function $g\in C(\partial \Omega)$ is also given and assumed to extend to a $C^3(\tir{\Omega})$ function $G$.

nodes.name: Hessian matrix and determinant operator
nodes.statement: In \eqref{MA}, $D^2 u=\big( \partial^2 u/(\partial x_i \partial x_j)\big)_{i,j=1,\ldots, 2} $ is the Hessian matrix of $u$ and $\det$ denotes the determinant operator.

nodes.name: Lagrange finite element space V_h and gradient
nodes.statement: Let $V_h$ denote the Lagrange finite element space of degree $k \geq 2$ and let $D v$ denote the gradient of the function $v$.

nodes.name: Cofactor matrix
nodes.statement: Recall that $\operatorname{cof} D^2 v$ denotes the matrix of cofactors of $D^2 v$.

nodes.name: C^0 interior penalty discretization of the Monge-Ampere equation (abstract form)
nodes.statement: The $C^0$ interior penalty discretization can be written in abstract form as: find $u_h \in V_h$ such that $u_h=g_h$ on $\partial \Omega$ and \begin{align} A(u_h,\phi) & = 0, \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega). \end{align} Here $g_h$ denotes the canonical interpolant in $V_h$ of a continuous extension of $g$ and $A$ is defined in \eqref{IP-form} below.
nodes.statement_short: Find $u_h \in V_h$ with boundary values $g_h$ such that $A(u_h,\phi)=0$ for all test functions.

nodes.name: Abstract interior penalty discrete problem
nodes.statement: A(u_h,\phi) & = 0, \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega).
nodes.label: IP-abstract

nodes.name: Frechet derivative A'(u;v,phi) of the interior penalty form
nodes.statement: The discretization has the property that if we denote by $A'(u;v, \phi)$ the Fr\'echet derivative evaluated at $u$ of the mapping $v \to A(v,\phi)$, then $A'(u;v,\phi)= \int_{\Omega} \big( (\operatorname{cof} D^2 u) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \,d x,$ which gives the weak form of a standard linear elliptic operator.
nodes.statement_short: Denotes by $A'(u;v,\phi)$ the Frechet derivative of $v\mapsto A(v,\phi)$ at $u$; at $u$ it is the weak form of a linear elliptic operator.

nodes.name: Existence of smooth solutions on smooth strictly convex domains
nodes.statement: It is known that when $\Omega$ is strictly convex with a smooth boundary, and with our smoothness assumptions on $f$ and $g$, \eqref{MA} has a smooth solution.
assumptions: $\Omega$ is strictly convex with a smooth boundary
with our smoothness assumptions on $f$ and $g$

nodes.name: Triangulation T_h
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}_h$ denote a conforming, shape regular and quasi-uniform triangulation of $\Omega$ into simplices $K$.

nodes.name: Edge sets of the triangulation
nodes.statement: We denote by $\mathcal{E}_h$ the set of edges of $\mathcal{T}_h$, by $\mathcal{E}^b_h$ the set of boundary edges and by $\mathcal{E}^i_h$ the set of interior edges.

nodes.name: Element diameter h_K and mesh size h
nodes.statement: Let $h_K$ denote the diameter of the element $K$ and put $h=\max_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} h_K$.

nodes.name: Mesh size bounded by one
nodes.statement: We assume that $0< h \leq 1$.

nodes.name: Shape regularity and quasi-uniformity constants
nodes.statement: We recall that, for a shape regular and quasi-uniform triangulation, there exists a constant $\sigma >0$ such that $h_K/\rho_K \leq \sigma$, for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$ where $\rho_K$ denotes the radius of the largest ball inside $K$ and there is another constant $C$ such that $h \leq C h_K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$.
assumptions: for a shape regular and quasi-uniform triangulation
conclusions: there exists a constant $\sigma >0$ such that $h_K/\rho_K \leq \sigma$, for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$
there is another constant $C$ such that $h \leq C h_K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$

nodes.name: Generic constant C
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper, we will use the letter $C$ for a generic constant, independent of $h$, which may change from occurrences.

nodes.name: Sobolev spaces W^{s,p}
nodes.statement: We use the usual notation $W^{s,p}(\Omega)$, $1 \leq s, p \leq \infty$ for the Sobolev spaces of functions in $L^{p}(\Omega)$, $1 \leq p \leq \infty$, with weak derivatives up to order $s$ in $L^{p}(\Omega)$.

nodes.name: Sobolev spaces H^s and H^1_0
nodes.statement: The standard notation $H^s(\Omega)$ is used for $W^{s,2}(\Omega)$ and $H^{1}_{0}(\Omega)$ denotes the subspace of elements in $H^1(\Omega)$ with vanishing trace on the boundary $\partial \Omega$.

nodes.name: Space W^{1,infty}_0
nodes.statement: Similarly, we define $W^{1,\infty}_{0}(\Omega)$.

nodes.name: Sobolev norm and seminorm notation
nodes.statement: The norm of $v \in W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ is denoted $\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ and its seminorm $|v|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$.

nodes.name: Polynomial space P_k(K)
nodes.statement: Denote by $P_k(K)$ the space of polynomials of degree $k$ on the element $K$.

nodes.name: Broken Sobolev norm
nodes.statement: We will need the broken Sobolev norm defined for $1 \leq p < \infty$ by \begin{equation*} \|v\|_{W^{k,p}({\mathcal T}_h)}=\left(\sum_{K \in {\mathcal T}_h}\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(K)}^p\right)^{1/p}, \end{equation*} and for $p=\infty$ by \begin{equation*} \|v\|_{W^{k,\infty}({\mathcal T}_h)}=\max_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h}\|v\|_{W^{k,\infty}(K)}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Elementwise Sobolev norm over $\mathcal{T}_h$: $\ell^p$-sum of local norms, or max for $p=\infty$.

nodes.name: Inverse estimates
nodes.statement: \|v\|_{W^{s,p}(\mathcal{T}_h)}\leq Ch^{t-s+\min(0,\frac{2}{p}-\frac{2}{q})}\|v\|_{W^{t,q}(\mathcal{T}_h)}, \forall v\in V_h,
assumptions: valid for $0\leq t \leq s$ and $1\leq p,q \leq \infty$
nodes.statement_short: Discrete functions satisfy inverse inequalities trading derivatives and integrability for powers of $h$.
nodes.label: inverse

nodes.name: Trace inequality
nodes.statement: We also recall the trace inequality \cite[Theorem 1.6.6]{Brenner08}, $\|v\|_{L^p(\partial \Omega)}\leq C \|v\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}, 1 \leq p \leq \infty$ which gives by a scaling argument \begin{equation} \|v\|_{L^p(\partial K)}\leq C h^{-\frac{1}{p}} (||v||_{L^p(K)} + h ||D v||_{L^p(K)} ). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Trace inequality $L^p(\partial\Omega)\lesssim W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, scaled to an element $K$.

nodes.name: Scaled trace estimate on an element
nodes.statement: \|v\|_{L^p(\partial K)}\leq C h^{-\frac{1}{p}} (||v||_{L^p(K)} + h ||D v||_{L^p(K)} ).
nodes.label: trace-estimate

nodes.name: Edge L1 norms bounded by W^{1,1} norm
nodes.statement: \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i} \|\phi\|_{L^1(e)} \leq C h^{-1} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h}\|\phi\|_{W^{1,1}(K)} =C h^{-1} \|\phi\|_{W^{1,1}}.
nodes.label: w11-phi

nodes.name: Trace inverse inequality
nodes.statement: ||v||_{L^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} ||v||_{L^2(K)} \, \forall v \in V_h.
nodes.label: trace-inverse

nodes.name: Lagrange interpolation error estimate
nodes.statement: ||v-I_h v||_{W^{s,p}(\mathcal{T}_h)} & \leq C h^{k+1-s} ||v||_{W^{k+1,p}}, s=0, 1, 2 \text{ and } 1\leq p \leq \infty, v \in W^{k+1,p}.
nodes.statement_short: Lagrange interpolant error in broken $W^{s,p}$ norm is $O(h^{k+1-s})$.
nodes.label: nodal-interpolant

nodes.name: Proof of the interpolation estimate
nodes.statement: This follows from our assumptions on the triangulation and \cite[ (4.4.5) ]{Brenner08}, i.e. for $ v \in W^{k+1,p}(K)$ \begin{equation} |v-I_h v|_{W^{s,p}(K)} \leq C h^{k+1-s}_K |v|_{W^{k+1,p}(K)}, s=0, 1, 2 \text{ and } 1\leq p \leq \infty. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Sum the local interpolation estimate (4.4.5) of Brenner-Scott using quasi-uniformity.

nodes.name: Local Lagrange interpolation estimate
nodes.statement: |v-I_h v|_{W^{s,p}(K)} \leq C h^{k+1-s}_K |v|_{W^{k+1,p}(K)}, s=0, 1, 2 \text{ and } 1\leq p \leq \infty.
nodes.label: local-nodal-interpolant

nodes.name: Trace estimate of the interpolation error gradient
nodes.statement: \begin{split} || D( I_h u - u) ||_{L^{2}(\partial K)} & \leq C h^{- \frac{1}{2} } || D( I_h u - u) ||_{L^{2}(K)} + C h^{ \frac{1}{2} } || D(I_h u - u) ||_{H^{1}(K)} \\ & \leq C h^{k- \frac{1}{2}} || u ||_{H^{k+1}(K)}. \end{split}
nodes.label: bramble

nodes.name: Frobenius inner product
nodes.statement: For two matrices $A$ and $B$, $A:B = \sum^2_{i,j=1}A_{ij}B_{ij}$ denotes their Frobenius inner product.

nodes.name: Divergence of a matrix field
nodes.statement: The divergence of a matrix field is understood as the vector obtained by taking the divergence of each row.

nodes.name: Determinant identity and Frechet derivative of det
nodes.statement: For $v$ sufficiently smooth we have \begin{equation} \det D^2 v = \frac{1}{2} (\operatorname{cof} D^2 v): D^2 v, \end{equation} and if $F(v) = \det D^2 v -f$, the Fr\'echet derivative of $F$ at $v$ is given by \begin{equation} F'(v) w = (\operatorname{cof} D^2 v): D^2 w, \end{equation} for $v,w$ sufficiently smooth.
conclusions: \det D^2 v = \frac{1}{2} (\operatorname{cof} D^2 v): D^2 v,
F'(v) w = (\operatorname{cof} D^2 v): D^2 w,
nodes.statement_short: $\det D^2v=\frac12\mathrm{cof}D^2v:D^2v$ and the derivative of $\det D^2 v - f$ is $w\mapsto \mathrm{cof}D^2v:D^2w$.

nodes.name: Determinant as half cofactor contraction
nodes.statement: \det D^2 v = \frac{1}{2} (\operatorname{cof} D^2 v): D^2 v,
nodes.label: det1

nodes.name: Frechet derivative of the Monge-Ampere operator
nodes.statement: F'(v) w = (\operatorname{cof} D^2 v): D^2 w,
nodes.label: det3

nodes.name: Divergence form of the cofactor contraction
nodes.statement: Under the same assumptions \begin{equation} \operatorname{div}\big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v )= (\operatorname{cof} D^2 w): D^2 v, \end{equation} which is a consequence of the product rule and the row divergence-free property of the Hessian, i.e. $\operatorname{div}( \operatorname{cof} D^2 w) =0$.
conclusions: \operatorname{div}\big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v )= (\operatorname{cof} D^2 w): D^2 v,

nodes.name: Divergence identity for cofactor matrix
nodes.statement: \operatorname{div}\big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v )= (\operatorname{cof} D^2 w): D^2 v,
nodes.label: det2

nodes.name: Linearized Monge-Ampere operator in divergence form
nodes.statement: F'(u)v= \operatorname{div} \big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 u) D v \big).
nodes.label: det4

nodes.name: Linearity of the cofactor in two dimensions
nodes.statement: \operatorname{cof}(D^2 v +D^2 w) = \operatorname{cof}(D^2 v) + \operatorname{cof}(D^2 w),
nodes.label: linearity

nodes.name: Difference of determinants
nodes.statement: \det D^2 v - \det D^2 w = \frac{1}{2} (\operatorname{cof}(D^2 v) + \operatorname{cof}(D^2 w)): (D^2 v - D^2 w).
nodes.label: det5

nodes.name: Difference of determinants in divergence form
nodes.statement: \det D^2 v - \det D^2 w = \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{div} \Big( \big( \operatorname{cof} D^2 (v+w)\big) D(v -w)\Big).
nodes.label: det6

nodes.name: Uniform positive definiteness of cof D^2 u
nodes.statement: We recall that $u$ is strictly convex and thus $\operatorname{cof} D^2 u $ is uniformly positive definite; that is, there exists positive constants $\alpha_0$ and $\alpha_1$ such that $\forall x \in \mathbb{R}^2$ \begin{equation} \alpha_0 |r|^2 \leq r^T (\operatorname{cof} D^2 u(x) ) r \leq \alpha_1 |r|^2, \quad \forall r \in \mathbb{R}^2. \end{equation}
conclusions: $\operatorname{cof} D^2 u $ is uniformly positive definite
nodes.statement_short: Strict convexity of $u$ gives constants $\alpha_0,\alpha_1>0$ bounding $\mathrm{cof}D^2u$ spectrally.

nodes.name: Ellipticity bounds for cof D^2 u
nodes.statement: \alpha_0 |r|^2 \leq r^T (\operatorname{cof} D^2 u(x) ) r \leq \alpha_1 |r|^2, \quad \forall r \in \mathbb{R}^2.
nodes.label: SPD

nodes.name: Discrete (elementwise) Hessian
nodes.statement: For $v \in V_h$, we will make the abuse of notation of denoting by $D^2v$ the discrete Hessian of $v$ computed element by element.

nodes.name: Outward normal and restriction
nodes.statement: For $e \subset \partial K$, let $n_K$ denote the outward normal to $K$ and let $v|_K$ denote the restriction of the field $v$ to $K$.

nodes.name: Jump and average of a vector field
nodes.statement: For $e=K^+ \cap K^-$, we define the jump of the vector field $v$ across $e$ as \begin{equation} \[v\]_e=v|_{K^+} \cdot n_{K^+} + v|_{K^-} \cdot n_{K^-}, \end{equation} and its average on $e$ as \begin{equation} \{\!\{v\}\!\}_e= \frac{1}{2}(v|_{K^+} + v|_{K^-} ). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Jump of a vector field is the sum of normal components from both sides; average is the arithmetic mean.

nodes.name: Jump and average of a matrix field
nodes.statement: The jump and average of a matrix field $E$ on $e$ are defined respectively as \begin{equation} \[E\]_e=n_{K^+}^T E|_{K^+} +n_{K^-}^T E|_{K^-}, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \{\!\{E\}\!\}_e= \frac{1}{2}(E|_{K^+} + E|_{K^-}). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Jump-average product identity
nodes.statement: For a matrix field $E$ and a vector field $v$ it is not difficult to check that for $e \in \mathcal{E}^i_h$ \begin{equation} \[Ev\]_e=\[\{\!\{E\}\!\}_e v\]_e+\[E\]_e\{\!\{v\}\!\}_e. \end{equation}
assumptions: a matrix field $E$ and a vector field $v$

nodes.name: Ritz projection hat P_h
nodes.statement: Let $\hat{P}_h:H_0^1(\Omega) \rightarrow V_h$ denote the projection with respect to the bilinear form $A'(u;\cdot,\cdot)$ and recall that $G$ denotes a $C^3(\tir{\Omega})$ extension of $g$.
differentia: with respect to the bilinear form $A'(u;\cdot,\cdot)$

nodes.name: Projection P_h with nonhomogeneous boundary values
nodes.statement: We define $$ P_h u = \hat{P}_h(u-G) + I_h G, $$ where $I_h$ denotes the canonical Lagrange interpolant operator into $V_h$.

nodes.name: Boundary values and Galerkin relation of P_h
nodes.statement: Then $P_h u = I_h u$ on $\partial \Omega$ and \begin{equation} A'(u;P_h u - u, \phi) = A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi) ,~ \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega). \end{equation}
conclusions: A'(u;P_h u - u, \phi) = A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi) ,~ \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega).

nodes.name: Galerkin orthogonality of P_h
nodes.statement: A'(u;P_h u - u, \phi) = A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi) ,~ \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega).
nodes.label: 2grid-proj-def

nodes.name: Proof of the W^{1,infty} projection estimate
nodes.statement: Put $w=u-G$. Since $w=0$ on $\partial \Omega$ and $w$ is smooth, we have \cite[Corollary 8.1.12]{Brenner08} \begin{equation*} ||w- \hat{P}_h(w)||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} ||w||_{W^{k+1,\infty}}, \ \text{for } w \in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega), w=0 \text{ on } \partial \Omega. \end{equation*} Therefore \begin{align*} ||u-P_h u||_{W^{1,\infty}} & = ||w+ G - \hat{P}_h w-I_h G ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \\ & \leq ||w- \hat{P}_h w||_{W^{1,\infty}} +||G-I_h G||_{W^{1,\infty}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split $u-P_hu$ into the Ritz-projection error of $w=u-G$ and the interpolation error of $G$; apply the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Reduce to Ritz projection of w
nodes.statement: Put $w=u-G$. Since $w=0$ on $\partial \Omega$ and $w$ is smooth, we have \cite[Corollary 8.1.12]{Brenner08} \begin{equation*} ||w- \hat{P}_h(w)||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} ||w||_{W^{k+1,\infty}}, \ \text{for } w \in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega), w=0 \text{ on } \partial \Omega. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Set $w=u-G$ and recall the Ritz projection $W^{1,\infty}$ estimate

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement: Therefore \begin{align*} ||u-P_h u||_{W^{1,\infty}} & = ||w+ G - \hat{P}_h w-I_h G ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \\ & \leq ||w- \hat{P}_h w||_{W^{1,\infty}} +||G-I_h G||_{W^{1,\infty}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split error into Ritz and interpolation parts

nodes.name: W^{1,infty} estimate of the Ritz projection
nodes.statement: Since $w=0$ on $\partial \Omega$ and $w$ is smooth, we have \cite[Corollary 8.1.12]{Brenner08} \begin{equation*} ||w- \hat{P}_h(w)||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} ||w||_{W^{k+1,\infty}}, \ \text{for } w \in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega), w=0 \text{ on } \partial \Omega. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: W^{1,infty} error of the projection P_h
nodes.statement: It thus follows from the approximation properties of $I_h$ that \begin{equation} ||u-P_h u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} ||u||_{W^{k+1,\infty}} \equiv C_1 h^k, \ \text{for } u \in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega). \end{equation}

nodes.name: W^{1,infty} projection estimate defining C_1
nodes.statement: ||u-P_h u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} ||u||_{W^{k+1,\infty}} \equiv C_1 h^k, \ \text{for } u \in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega).
nodes.label: 2grid-proj1

nodes.name: Broken W^{2,infty} error of the projection P_h

nodes.name: Proof of the W^{1,1} Green's function bound
nodes.statement: It is enough to prove that $|G^z_h |_{W^{1,1}} \leq C|\ln h|$ which follows from the bound $| G^z_h |_{W^{1,2}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} $ and H\"older's inequality. nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: For $w,v \in H^2(K)$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$ we have \begin{multline*} A(w+v,\phi)-A(w,\phi)= -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \big(\det D^2(w+v)-\det D^2w\big)\phi\,d x \\+ \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 (w+v) \}\!\} D (w+v) \] \phi \,d s - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 w \}\!\} D w \] \phi \,d s, \end{multline*} for all $\phi \in H^1_0(\Omega)$. Since $D^2 w$ is a $2 \times 2$ matrix, $\det D^2(w+v)= \det D^2 w + \det D^2 v +\operatorname{cof} D^2 w : D^2 v$. Thus \begin{multline*} A(w+v,\phi)-A(w,\phi)= -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} (\det D^2v)\phi\,d x -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} (\operatorname{cof} D^2 w: D^2v)\phi\,d x \\+ \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi\,d s + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi\,d s. + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D v \] \phi\,d s. \end{multline*} By \eqref{det2} $\operatorname{cof} D^2 w: D^2 v = \operatorname{div}\big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v )$. This implies that \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \operatorname{div} \big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v\big) \phi \,d x + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi \,d s \\ & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \,d s, \end{align*} and $R(w;v,\phi)$ is given by \eqref{rdef1}. By integration by parts and using the fact $\phi=0$ on $\partial \Omega$, \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \,d x - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v \] \phi \,d x \\ & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi \,d s + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \,d s . \end{align*} By \eqref{jumpaverage}, $ \[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v\] = \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] + \[\operatorname{cof} D^2 w\] \{\!\{D v\}\!\}. $ It follows that \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K }\big( (\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \,d x - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 w)\] \{\!\{D v\}\!\} \phi \,d s \\\notag & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \,d s . \end{align*} Finally, since by assumption $u \in C^3(\Omega)$, $\[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 u)\]=0$. In addition, by definition $\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\}$ is continuous and $Du$ is continuous by the assumption on $u$. Thus $\[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D u \]=0$ on each interior edge. The statement about $A'(u;v,\phi)$ easily follows.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{det1} and integration by parts \begin{multline*} \int_{K} (\det D^2 v ) \phi \,d x = \frac{1}{2} \int_{K} (\operatorname{cof} D^2 v ): (D^2 v) \, \phi \,d x = \frac{1}{2} \int_{K} \operatorname{div}\big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 v) D v ) \phi \,d x \\ =- \frac{1}{2} \int_K [(\operatorname{cof} D^2 v) D v ] \cdot D \phi \,d x + \frac{1}{2} \int_{\partial K} \big[ (\operatorname{cof} D^2 v) D v \big] \cdot n_K \phi \,d s. \end{multline*} By definition of jump and since $\phi=0$ on $\partial \Omega$, we have \begin{align} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{\partial K} \big( (\operatorname{cof} D^2 v) D v \big) \cdot n_K \phi \,d s & = \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 v) D v \] \phi \,d s . \end{align} We conclude that \begin{multline*} R(w;v,\phi) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_K [(\operatorname{cof} D^2 v) D v ] \cdot D \phi \,d x -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 v) D v \] \phi \,d s \\ + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D v \] \phi\,d s. \end{multline*} Therefore, using \eqref{jumpaverage} to expand the term $\[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 v) D v \] $ we obtain \eqref{R1-simple}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: For $v_h \in B_h$, we have using \eqref{Phi-def} and \eqref{2grid-proj-def} \begin{align*} \begin{split} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) &= A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- v_h,\phi)+A'(u; v_h- P_h u,\phi) \\ &= -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) + A'(u; u - P_h u,\phi) \\ &= -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) - A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). \end{split} \end{align*} By definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, and since $A(u,\phi)=0$, we have $$ -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) = A(u,\phi) -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) = -R(u;v_h-u,\phi). $$ We conclude that \begin{align} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) = -R(u;v_h-u,\phi) - A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). \end{align} Therefore, using \eqref{R1-simple}, \eqref{w11-phi} and \eqref{Frechet-at-u}, we have \begin{multline*} | A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) | \leq C || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} \\ +C || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } || \phi ||_{L^1(e)} + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi) | \\ \leq C h^{-1} || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)|. \end{multline*} By definition of $B_h$, $||v_h-u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} |\ln h |$. Thus \begin{multline*} | A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) | \leq C h^{k-2} |\ln h | \, || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} h^{k} |\ln h | + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)| \\ \leq (C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 ) h^{k} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} + | A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)| . \end{multline*} Taking $\phi=g^z_{h,i}$ with the estimate \eqref{2grid-W11greenbound}, and taking $\phi=G^z_h$ with the estimate \eqref{green-0}, we obtain using the definition of $C_4$ $$ \|\Phi( v_h)- P_h u\|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq (C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 + C_4 ) h^{k } |\ln h|. $$ Since $C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 \leq C_4$ for $h$ sufficiently small and $k \geq 3$, we get $\|\Phi( v_h)- P_h u\|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq 2 C_4 h^{k } |\ln h|$. By triangular inequality and \eqref{2grid-proj1}, the result follows.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.7
nodes.statement: The proof is based on the expression \eqref{expr-con} of $A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi)$ derived in the proof of Lemma \ref{contraction} and the expression \eqref{expr-inv} of $A'(u; \Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi )$ derived in the proof of Lemma \ref{invariant}. Since $\Phi(u_h) = u_h$, we have \begin{align} \begin{split} A'(u; u_h - P_h u,\phi) & = A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - P_h u,\phi) \\ & = A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi) + A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi). \end{split} \end{align} In view of \eqref{expr-con}, we obtain \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C ||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} ||P_h u-u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + \\ C ||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h- P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C ||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \\ + C ||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)}. \end{multline} By an inverse estimate, Theorem \ref{2grid-imp-thm}, triangle inequality and \eqref{2grid-proj1}, we have $||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| $. Similarly, using \eqref{2grid-proj2}, we have $||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h|$. Next, by the scaled trace inverse inequality \eqref{trace-inverse} and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality \begin{multline} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{-1} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}( K)} ||\phi||_{H^1( K)} \\ \leq C h^{-1} || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline} By \eqref{bramble}, an inverse estimate and \eqref{local-nodal-interpolant} \begin{align*} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} & \leq | P_h u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} + | I_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} \\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)}\\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)}. \end{align*} We have $|| P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k ||u||_{H^{k+1}}$. This follows from \cite[Theorem 5.4.4]{Brenner08} in the case of homogeneous boundary conditions. The proof of the general case is similar to \eqref{2grid-proj1}. Thus $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ^2 \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} \leq C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}}. $$ As with \eqref{u-p-03}, by \eqref{trace-inverse} and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, it follows that \begin{multline} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2} } \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{H^1( K)} \\ \leq C h^{k-1} ||u||_{H^{k+1} } ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline} We conclude from \eqref{u-p-02}--\eqref{u-p-04} that \begin{multline*} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| \, || P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-1} | \ln h| \, || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-1} ||u_h - P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-2} | \ln h| \, || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline*} Therefore since by Theorem \ref{2grid-imp-thm} we have the suboptimal estimate $ || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} \leq C ||u_h - P_h u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^k | \ln h| $ \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-1} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-2} | \ln h| h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-2} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}\\ \leq C h^{k-2} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} \leq C h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}, \end{multline} for $k \geq 3$. By \eqref{expr-inv}, we have $$ A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) = -R(u;P_h u-u,\phi) + A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). $$ Using \eqref{R1-simple} and inverse estimates as for \eqref{u-p-04}, we obtain \begin{multline*} | A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) | \leq C ||P_h u - u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} ||P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} ||P_h u - u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} +C\|I_hG-G\|_{H^1}\|\phi\|_{H^1}, \end{multline*} i.e. \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) | \leq C ( h^{k-1} |\ln h| h^k + h^{k-2} |\ln h| h^k + h^k ) ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ \leq C h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}, \end{multline} for $k \geq 3$. Taking $\phi = u_h - P_h u $ in \eqref{u-p-01} and using \eqref{u-p-05} and \eqref{u-p-06}, we get from Poincar\'e's inequality and $k \geq 3$, for $h$ sufficiently small $$ || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} \leq Ch^k. $$ This completes the proof by a triangle inequality.

nodes.statement: We have the estimate \begin{equation} ||u^h-u_h||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k, \end{equation} for $k \geq 3, H=h^{\lambda}, 1> \lambda> 1/2 + (2+\epsilon)/(2k), 0< \epsilon <1$ and $h$ sufficiently small.
nodes.statement_short: With coarse size $H=h^\lambda$, $\lambda>1/2+(2+\epsilon)/(2k)$, the two-grid solution is within $O(h^k)$ of $u_h$ in $H^1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.1
nodes.statement: By definition of the two-grid algorithm, the definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, and $A(u_h,\phi)=0$ for $\phi \in V_h\cap W^{1,\infty}_0(\Omega)$, we have \begin{align*} A'(u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi)&= A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_H-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A(u_H,\phi) \\ & = A(u_h,\phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi) = - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*} It follows that \begin{align*} A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi)& = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*} With arguments similar to the ones used in the proof of Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm}, we have \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C || \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)}\\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline} But, using \eqref{bramble}, \eqref{local-nodal-interpolant} and an inverse estimate \begin{align*} | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} & \leq | u - I_H u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} + | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}( K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}( K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} ( K)}. \end{align*} It follows that $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} }. $$ We therefore obtain from \eqref{nodal-interpolant} and Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}}. $$ By Cauchy-Schwarz's inequality, \eqref{trace-inverse} and an inverse estimate, it follows that $$ \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{- \frac{3}{2}} H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}}. $$ Therefore, since $|| u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C H^{k-1} |\ln H|$ and by the discrete Sobolev inequality, c.f. \cite{Bramble86}, $|| \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \leq C (1+ | \ln h|^{ 1/2 }) ||\phi||_{H^1}$, we obtain from \eqref{u-p-066} \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} | \ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||u||_{H^{k+1} } ||\phi||_{H^1} + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \\ \leq C h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline} Using \eqref{R1-simple} and the trace estimates \eqref{trace-inverse} and \eqref{trace-estimate}, we have \begin{multline} |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \leq C || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ \leq C h^{-2} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline} Taking $\phi = u_h - u^h $ in \eqref{u-p-07} and using \eqref{u-p-08}, we get from Poincar\'e's inequality, Theorems \ref{2grid-imp-thm} and \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} for $k \geq 3$ and $h$ sufficiently small \begin{multline*} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C (h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| + H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| ) || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \\ +C h^{-2} (h^{k} |\ln h | + H^{k} |\ln H |) (h^k+H^k). \end{multline*} We conclude that for $H=h^{\lambda}$, $\lambda > \max \{1/(k-1), 3/(2k-1) \} = 3/(2k-1)$ and $k \geq 3$, $$ || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^{-2} |\ln H \, | H^{2k}. $$ We therefore get $||u^h-u_h||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k$ provided $\lambda > 3/(2k-1)$ and $2 \lambda k -2- \epsilon > k$ for some $\epsilon \in (0,1) $, that is $\lambda > \max \{ (k+2+ \epsilon)/(2k), 3/(2k-1) \} = 1/2 + (2+\epsilon)/(2k)$ for $k \geq 3$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $A'(u;u_h-u^h,\phi)$ as a coefficient perturbation plus a remainder, bound with trace/inverse estimates and Theorems 3.6-3.7. Key step: choose $\lambda$ so the perturbation term absorbs and the remainder is $O(h^k)$.

nodes.name: Residual identity
nodes.statement: By definition of the two-grid algorithm, the definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, and $A(u_h,\phi)=0$ for $\phi \in V_h\cap W^{1,\infty}_0(\Omega)$, we have \begin{align*} A'(u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi)&= A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_H-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A(u_H,\phi) \\ & = A(u_h,\phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi) = - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Express $A'(u_H;u_h-u^h,\phi)$ as a remainder

nodes.name: Change linearization point
nodes.statement: It follows that \begin{align*} A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi)& = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Switch the linearization from $u_H$ to $u$

nodes.name: Initial bound
nodes.statement: With arguments similar to the ones used in the proof of Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm}, we have \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C || \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)}\\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Bound as in the proof of Theorem 3.7

nodes.name: Boundary seminorm of u-u_H
nodes.statement: But, using \eqref{bramble}, \eqref{local-nodal-interpolant} and an inverse estimate \begin{align*} | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} & \leq | u - I_H u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} + | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}( K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}( K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} ( K)}. \end{align*} It follows that $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} }. $$ We therefore obtain from \eqref{nodal-interpolant} and Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound elementwise boundary seminorm of $u-u_H$ using Theorem 3.7 on the coarse mesh

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: By Cauchy-Schwarz's inequality, \eqref{trace-inverse} and an inverse estimate, it follows that $$ \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{- \frac{3}{2}} H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz, trace inverse and inverse estimates

nodes.name: Refined bound
nodes.statement: Therefore, since $|| u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C H^{k-1} |\ln H|$ and by the discrete Sobolev inequality, c.f. \cite{Bramble86}, $|| \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \leq C (1+ | \ln h|^{ 1/2 }) ||\phi||_{H^1}$, we obtain from \eqref{u-p-066} \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} | \ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||u||_{H^{k+1} } ||\phi||_{H^1} + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \\ \leq C h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Use discrete Sobolev inequality to get (4.3)

nodes.name: Remainder bound
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{R1-simple} and the trace estimates \eqref{trace-inverse} and \eqref{trace-estimate}, we have \begin{multline} |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \leq C || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ \leq C h^{-2} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the remainder at $u_H$

nodes.name: Test with u_h-u^h
nodes.statement: Taking $\phi = u_h - u^h $ in \eqref{u-p-07} and using \eqref{u-p-08}, we get from Poincar\'e's inequality, Theorems \ref{2grid-imp-thm} and \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} for $k \geq 3$ and $h$ sufficiently small \begin{multline*} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C (h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| + H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| ) || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \\ +C h^{-2} (h^{k} |\ln h | + H^{k} |\ln H |) (h^k+H^k). \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Test, apply Poincare and Theorems 3.6-3.7

nodes.name: Choose lambda
nodes.statement: We conclude that for $H=h^{\lambda}$, $\lambda > \max \{1/(k-1), 3/(2k-1) \} = 3/(2k-1)$ and $k \geq 3$, $$ || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^{-2} |\ln H \, | H^{2k}. $$ We therefore get $||u^h-u_h||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k$ provided $\lambda > 3/(2k-1)$ and $2 \lambda k -2- \epsilon > k$ for some $\epsilon \in (0,1) $, that is $\lambda > \max \{ (k+2+ \epsilon)/(2k), 3/(2k-1) \} = 1/2 + (2+\epsilon)/(2k)$ for $k \geq 3$.
nodes.statement_short: Absorb and choose $\lambda$ to get $O(h^k)$

nodes.name: Bound on A'(u;u_h-u^h,phi)
nodes.statement: | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C || \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)}\\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|.
nodes.label: u-p-066

nodes.name: Exponential test problem on the unit square
nodes.statement: The computational domain is taken to be the unit square $[0,1]^2$. A uniform grid is obtained by dividing the domain into smaller equal size squares, then dividing each square into two triangles by taking the diagonal with positive slope. We consider a smooth convex test function $u(x,y)=e^{(x^2+y^2)/2}$ so that $f(x,y)=(1+x^2+y^2)e^{(x^2+y^2)}$ and $g(x,y)=e^{(x^2+y^2)/2}$ on $\partial \Omega$.
nodes.statement_short: Test problem on $[0,1]^2$ with exact solution $u=e^{(x^2+y^2)/2}$ on a uniform diagonal triangulation.

nodes.name: Convergence for quadratic elements
nodes.statement: While our convergence analysis is only for cubic and higher order elements, we believe the results should be true for quadratic elements.

nodes.name: Coarse-grid Newton solver with Poisson initial guess
nodes.statement: On the coarse grid of size $H$, we first seek an initial guess $u_H^0$ of $u_H$ as the standard finite element approximation of the solution $u_0$ of \begin{equation*} \Delta u_0=2\sqrt{f}, \quad u_0=g \text{ on } \partial \Omega. \end{equation*} For solving the coarse grid problem, we perform Newton's method on the coarse grid, setting the maximum iterations to 10 and we impose that the algorithm terminates when $\|u_H\|_{L^{\infty}}/ \|u^0_H\|_{L^{\infty}} \leq 10^{-6}.$
nodes.statement_short: Initialize with the FE solution of $\Delta u_0=2\sqrt f$, then run at most 10 Newton iterations with a relative stopping test.

nodes.name: Initial guess from Poisson problem
nodes.statement: On the coarse grid of size $H$, we first seek an initial guess $u_H^0$ of $u_H$ as the standard finite element approximation of the solution $u_0$ of \begin{equation*} \Delta u_0=2\sqrt{f}, \quad u_0=g \text{ on } \partial \Omega. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Newton iterations with stopping criterion
nodes.statement: For solving the coarse grid problem, we perform Newton's method on the coarse grid, setting the maximum iterations to 10 and we impose that the algorithm terminates when $\|u_H\|_{L^{\infty}}/ \|u^0_H\|_{L^{\infty}} \leq 10^{-6}.$

nodes.name: Two-grid computations are accurate and fast
nodes.statement: The two-grid computations are accurate and fast compared with Newton's method.
conclusions: The two-grid computations are accurate and fast compared with Newton's method.
